title: Projective Bell-locality threshold of two-qubit Werner states
source: Acín, Gisin, and Toner prove in Theorem~1 that $v_c=1/K_G(3)$, where $K_G(3)$ is the real Grothendieck constant of order three. Determining that constant would give the exact visibility threshold \sourcecite{ref:d8-03-agt06}{AGT06}.
progress: Designolle et al. construct a local model for all projective measurement directions up to a visibility of approximately $0.6875$. Their Eq.~(4) gives a certified lower bound on $v_c$ \sourcecite{ref:d8-03-dib-23}{DIB+23}.

Márton et al. certify the classical bound of a Bell inequality and report a three-dimensional quantum-to-classical ratio of approximately $1.438746$ in Table~4. The reciprocal gives an upper bound of approximately $0.69505$ on $v_c$ \sourcecite{ref:d8-03-mbdv26}{MBDV26}.

references.label: ref:d8-03-agt06
references.tex: A. Acín, N. Gisin, and B. Toner, ``Grothendieck's constant and local models for noisy entangled quantum states,'' (2006). \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0606138}{arXiv:quant-ph/0606138}.

references.label: ref:d8-03-dib-23
references.tex: S. Designolle, G. Iommazzo, M. Besançon, S. Knebel, P. Gelß, and S. Pokutta, ``Improved local models and new Bell inequalities via Frank-Wolfe algorithms,'' (2023). \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04721v4}{arXiv:2302.04721v4}.

comment: The related \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_2982ddd94453b5b6/}{Werner-state steering threshold} concerns one-sided steering with arbitrary measurements in higher dimensions. The catalog and literature were checked through November 26, 2026.
